Done. `/work/putnam_2002_b5.lean` compiles with exit 0, no errors, and no `sorry` warning. The only output is deprecation warnings from Mathlib names I used. The imports, statement, and header are unchanged, and the file contains no `sorry`, `axiom`, or `native_decide`.

**Construction:** Let N = 2002! · 2003³ and n = N². For j = 1..2002, write N = j·(b+1) with b = N/j − 1. Then n = j² + b·(2j² + b·j²), so the base-b digits are [j², 2j², j²]. That is a 3-digit palindrome as long as 2j² < b, which holds because b ≥ 2003³ − 1 and 2·2002² is far smaller. The 2002 values of b are distinct because j ↦ N/j is injective on 1..2002, so the set has at least 2002 elements.

The proof is written as a general lemma over any F satisfying "F = j·m with m ≥ 1 for each j ≤ 2002", then applied with F = 2002!.
